title: What's the Difference Between an Architect and a Designer?
excerpt: Most homeowners don't know the real difference between hiring an architect and hiring a designer. Here's what you need to know when planning your Westchester home project.
content:
When you're planning a home renovation or addition, you'll hear the terms "architect" and "designer" used pretty interchangeably. But they're not the same thing, and that distinction matters more than you might think. Understanding the difference can save you headaches and make sure your project gets built right the first time.

The main difference comes down to licensing and legal responsibility. A licensed architect in New York has completed years of education, passed rigorous exams, and carries liability insurance. An architect can legally sign off on plans and take responsibility for structural and code compliance. A designer, on the other hand, creates beautiful spaces but doesn't have those credentials or legal authority. Both can be talented. Only one can guarantee your project meets building code.

Why Your Architect Needs to Be a General Contractor Too

Here's where it gets practical. You can hire the best architect in Scarsdale or Rye to draw perfect plans. But if that architect has never actually built anything, there's a gap between the vision and the reality. Construction costs money. Materials have real limitations. Crews need clear direction on site.

The smartest move is working with someone who is both. A licensed architect in Westchester who is also a general contractor understands the entire process from paper to completion. Silvio Luca brings both credentials to every project. He's not just drawing plans and handing them off. He's the principal on the job, which means he's thinking about constructability from day one. Your kitchen remodel in White Plains gets designed with actual installation experience. Your second-story addition in Bronxville gets engineered by someone who has framed dozens of them.

The Difference Shows in Home Renovations and Additions

When you're doing a home renovation in Westchester County, permitting matters. Every town from Eastchester to Tarrytown has its own building department. You need plans that will pass inspection the first time, not get sent back for revisions. An architect knows what each inspector is looking for.

Home additions in Westchester require more than just good aesthetics. Your new primary suite in Larchmont needs to connect properly to existing systems. The open-concept conversion in Pelham Manor has to maintain the home's structural integrity. The historic restoration in Hastings-on-Hudson needs to respect what's already there while meeting current code. A residential architect in Westchester with hands-on building experience catches problems before they become expensive mistakes.

Building a Custom Home Means You Need Both Skills

If you're building a custom home in Westchester County from the ground up, you need someone who can visualize what you want and actually build it. That takes both design talent and construction knowledge. A general contractor in Westchester without design training will build what you ask for. A designer without building experience will create something that costs more than expected or can't be built as drawn.

When both skills are in one person, you get clarity, honesty, and a finished home that actually works.
